intro: Journalists often earn low wages because of systemic shifts in media ownership and the rise of precarious freelance work. This environment leaves many professionals without the business training needed to manage irregular income effectively.
tldr: Most journalists supplement their income because industry pay structures have collapsed.
Financial stress is a top cause of burnout in newsrooms today.
You can stabilize your income by treating your work as a small business.
Use Mac native tools to track expenses and automate your budget.

blocks.text: The root cause of financial precarity

The question of why do journalists make so little is rarely about the value of the work itself. It is about the collapse of traditional advertising models that once funded newsrooms. As media companies downsized, they moved toward contract labor. This forces journalists to act as business owners without the necessary training. You are now responsible for your own taxes, health insurance, and retirement. This transition creates a gap between your creative output and your financial security.
Managing your income as a business

To stop the cycle of living paycheck to paycheck, you must track every cent. Use a Mac native app like Banktivity to see your total net worth. If you prefer zero based budgeting, YNAB is a standard choice. These apps help you see where your money goes. They also highlight when your income does not match your expenses. You cannot fix what you do not measure.
Always keep business and personal finances separate. Open a dedicated business checking account for your freelance invoices. It makes tax season much easier.
blocks.title: Separate your funds

blocks.text: Journalism requires constant focus. Spending hours on spreadsheets takes away from your reporting time. Use macOS features to speed up your routine. You can use Apple Shortcuts to log expenses from your phone to a Numbers file. This keeps your records updated without manual entry.

Financial insecurity acts as a constant background task for your brain. It consumes cognitive energy that you need for deep reporting. When you worry about rent, you are less likely to take risks on investigative stories. This leads to burnout. You end up relying on easy, low-paid work to stay afloat. Breaking this cycle requires a plan that prioritizes your long-term stability over short-term survival.

faq.question: Why do journalists make so little compared to other professions?
faq.answer: The industry has shifted to a freelance-heavy model without providing the business infrastructure or benefits that come with traditional employment.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to manage my finances?
faq.answer: Lazur helps you navigate your finance apps, set reminders, and dictate notes about expenses, but it does not perform financial transactions or manage your bank accounts.

faq.question: What is the first step to financial stability?
faq.answer: Start by tracking your monthly expenses for three months to identify exactly how much you need to survive, then build a small emergency fund.

costs.title: Mental burnout
costs.text: Constant worry about money reduces your ability to focus on complex investigations.

costs.title: Limited career growth
costs.text: Without savings, you cannot invest in your own skills or professional equipment.

causes.title: Gig economy shift
causes.text: Newsrooms have outsourced labor, leaving journalists to manage their own business operations.

causes.title: Inconsistent cash flow
causes.text: Freelance payments are often delayed, making it hard to budget effectively.

causes.title: Lack of business training
causes.text: Journalism schools often ignore the financial realities of running an independent career.

fixes.title: Zero based budgeting
fixes.text: Assign every dollar a job before the month begins to prevent overspending.

fixes.title: Automated savings
fixes.text: Set up an automatic transfer to a high-yield savings account for taxes and emergencies.

fixes.title: Invoice tracking
fixes.text: Create a simple spreadsheet to track when invoices are sent and when they are due.
